title: Evening tape vault entry with a spare card

provenance.notes: Development family authored offline by a Claude agent from seed F05 in cases/dev/seed-plan.json (D-014), hard level. A two-person tape vault opened with the subject's badge and a spare card released under his PIN, while the other rostered operator had lost vault access in an administrative review. The corroboration path combines the spare-card register with the door camera counts (exchange 5), then the badge events and the colleague's statement. prompt_sha256 covers the content rules, kit sources src_f01.py to src_f03.py and the canonical seed.

facts.statement: Rafael Strand and Tobias Grell were the two operators rostered on the 14:00-22:30 shift at Westbrook Data Hall on 24 March 2026.
Shift supervisor Hester Vane was off site at the Marlow Road annex generator test from 19:30 to 23:00.
Tape Vault TV-1 opens only when two different credentials with TV-1 access are presented at its reader within 15 seconds.
Spare card SP-3, like the other spare cards in the NOC key cabinet, carried TV-1 access.
At 18:00 on 24 March the quarterly TV-1 access review removed TV-1 access from Grell's badge.
Grell's manager had approved his annual TV-1 access renewal on 19 March, but Credential Services did not enter it until 08:40 on 25 March.
The weekly full backup finished at 20:41 instead of about 13:00, after a tape drive fault at 11:20.
The 21:14 entry was the only evening-shift entry to TV-1 between 1 and 24 March 2026, although courier tape pulls are normally made on the day shift.
At 21:08 spare card SP-3 was released from the NOC key cabinet under Strand's PIN.
At 21:14 Strand's badge and spare card SP-3 were the two credentials presented at the TV-1 reader, four seconds apart, and the vault door opened.
The TV-1 door was opened from inside with the exit button at 21:51.
The nightly credential reconciliation at 06:00 on 25 March attributed both credentials of the 21:14 TV-1 entry to Strand.
The NOC key cabinet records a released spare card against the PIN that released it.
The Fernhill Archive Couriers driver collected the 14 courier tapes at 21:58.
The NOC key cabinet releases a spare card only against the PIN of a person whose badge opens TV-1.
At 20:45 Vane phoned the NOC from the annex and asked Strand to pull the 14 courier tapes from TV-1 before the 22:00 pickup.
Strand left the building through the lobby turnstile at 22:36.
Strand and Grell both held current TV-1 vault-handling certification on 24 March 2026.
At 21:07 the NOC key cabinet refused Grell's PIN for a spare card because his badge no longer opened TV-1.
Strand released SP-3 under his own PIN so that Grell could carry it.
Strand wrote Grell's name as the holder of SP-3 on the paper spare-card register, with the time and the reason.
Grell carried SP-3 and presented it at the TV-1 reader at 21:14, after Strand presented his own badge.
Grell and Strand pulled the 14 courier tapes together in TV-1 and left the vault together at 21:51.
The TV-1 door camera counted two people entering at 21:14 and two people leaving at 21:51.
Grell returned SP-3 to the NOC key cabinet at 22:05.
Grell left the building through the lobby turnstile at 22:31.
Grell left the building through the lobby turnstile at 20:32 and did not return that night.
During the 20:45 call Strand did not tell Vane that Grell had gone home.
Strand wanted the tapes on the 22:00 courier because Vane had given him a written reminder on 10 March after the 3 March tapes missed their courier.
At 21:14 Strand presented his own badge and then spare card SP-3 at the TV-1 reader himself, so that he could enter the vault alone.
Strand did not write a holder's name for SP-3 on the paper spare-card register.
Strand worked in TV-1 alone from 21:14 to 21:51.
Strand pulled the 14 courier tapes from TV-1 for the 22:00 courier.
The TV-1 door camera counted one person entering at 21:14 and one person leaving at 21:51.
Strand returned SP-3 to the NOC key cabinet at 22:05.

initial_documents.title: Access exception report, Tape Vault TV-1, 24 March 2026

content.body: Generated 25 March 2026 at 06:00 by the nightly credential reconciliation (Security Operations). TV-1 has a two-credential reader: the door opens only when two different credentials with TV-1 access are presented within 15 seconds. The reconciliation attributes a released spare card to the PIN that released it until the paper spare-card register is checked; the register has not been checked yet. Both credentials of the 21:14 entry are therefore attributed to R. Strand. Exception: possible single-person entry to a two-person area. Pattern note: this is the only evening-shift TV-1 entry between 1 and 24 March 2026; courier tape pulls are normally made on the day shift, at about 13:30. TV-1 is left by an exit button, which records no credential. The table lists TV-1 events and spare-card releases and returns; refused cabinet requests are not part of the reconciliation.

rows: Released under the PIN of R. Strand

initial_documents.title: Tape Vault TV-1 rules (Data Hall Security Standard 7.3)

content.body: (a) Work in TV-1 needs two people who each hold current vault-handling certification. Each presents a different credential at the two-credential reader, and both stay until the work is finished and leave together. (b) No person may present more than one credential at the reader. (c) Spare cards are kept in the NOC key cabinet, which releases a card only against the PIN of a person whose badge opens TV-1. A certified operator may release a spare card for a certified colleague whose own badge will not open TV-1, and must write the holder's name, the time and the reason on the paper spare-card register. The holder keeps the card until it is returned to the cabinet.

evaluator_packet.synopsis: Grell's TV-1 access came off his badge at 18:00 in the quarterly review because Credential Services had not entered his approved renewal. The weekly backup finished late, at 20:41, so Vane, off site, phoned at 20:45 and asked Strand to pull the 14 courier tapes before the 22:00 pickup. The key cabinet refused Grell's PIN, so Strand released spare card SP-3 under his own PIN for Grell and wrote Grell's name, the time and the reason on the paper register, as Standard 7.3(c) allows for a certified colleague. At the reader Strand presented his badge and Grell presented SP-3; they pulled the tapes together and left together at 21:51, and Grell returned the card at 22:05. Misleading circumstances: Grell's lapsed TV-1 access, the evening timing of the entry, and the reconciliation attributing both credentials to Strand.

evidence_artifacts.title: Written statement, Tobias Grell, Data Center Operator (26 March 2026)

content.body: My TV-1 access came off my badge at 18:00 on 24 March in the quarterly review; my renewal had not been entered. After Hester's call Rafael and I went to get the courier tapes out. At 21:07 the key cabinet refused my PIN, so Rafael released SP-3 on his PIN and wrote my name in the register as the holder. At the vault Rafael presented his badge and I presented SP-3. We pulled the fourteen tapes together and left together at about ten to ten. After the courier left I put SP-3 back in the cabinet, and I went home at the end of the shift.

evidence_artifacts.description: Statement from the second operator rostered on the 24 March evening shift, written for the review office.

evidence_artifacts.title: Written statement, Hester Vane, Shift Supervisor (25 March 2026)

content.body: I left for the generator test at the Marlow Road annex at 19:30 and was there until 23:00. The weekly backup ran late after a tape drive fault and finished at 20:41, so the courier tapes could not be pulled on the day shift. At 20:45 I phoned the NOC from the annex and Rafael answered. I asked him to get the fourteen courier tapes out of TV-1 before the 22:00 pickup. Tobias Grell was rostered with him, so I did not arrange anyone else. The courier confirmed collection of fourteen tapes at 21:58. I did not hear from either operator again that night.

evidence_artifacts.title: Credential Services record, TV-1 access renewal, T. Grell

content.body: Annual TV-1 access renewal for T. Grell approved by his manager, K. Osei, on 19 March 2026. Not entered before the quarterly TV-1 access review at 18:00 on 24 March (entry backlog of 11 renewals). Entered 25 March 2026 at 08:40; TV-1 access restored. Vault-handling certification current until 30 November 2026.

evidence_artifacts.description: Credential Services history of the annual TV-1 access renewal for badge 47710 (T. Grell), with approval and entry dates.

material_contradictions.description: The reconciliation attributes both credentials of the 21:14 entry to Strand, which looks like one person opening a two-person vault against Standard 7.3(b).
material_contradictions.resolution: The cabinet records a spare card against the releasing PIN. Strand released SP-3 for Grell, who carried it and presented it himself; two people went in and two came out.

material_contradictions.description: Grell's TV-1 access had been removed at 18:00, so the second credential could not have been his own badge.
material_contradictions.resolution: The removal was an entry backlog on a renewal approved on 19 March, and Standard 7.3(c) lets a certified colleague whose badge will not open TV-1 carry a released spare card.

material_contradictions.description: The entry was the only evening-shift TV-1 entry in March, outside the usual day-shift courier pull.
material_contradictions.resolution: The weekly full backup finished at 20:41, so the courier tapes could only be pulled in the evening, and Vane asked for them at 20:45.

decisive_support.description: The paper register shows SP-3 released by Strand to holder Grell at 21:08 with the reason, and the door camera counted two people in at 21:14 and two out at 21:51, matching Strand's account that Grell carried and presented SP-3.
Grell's statement gives the same account, and the badge events show both badges at the basement corridor door at 21:12 and Grell in the building until 22:31.

unsupported_grounds: The reconciliation attributing both credentials to Strand before the paper register is checked
Grell's TV-1 access having been removed at 18:00
The entry being the only evening-shift TV-1 entry in March

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: The other rostered operator carried SP-3 and presented it at the reader himself.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the paper spare-card register and the door camera counts; compare the holder and the person counts with the account.

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: One person presented both credentials and worked in the vault alone.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the camera counts, the evening badge events and the other operator's statement; check who was still in the building after 20:30.

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: The other operator's lapsed vault access made his part in the entry unauthorized.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the Credential Services record and read Standard 7.3(c) on spare cards for a certified colleague.

dimension_notes.clarity_neutrality: Credit open, single questions about the spare card and the people at the reader. 'Why did you use two cards?' presumes that one person presented both credentials.
dimension_notes.response_relevance: An answer to 'What was SP-3 released for?' that gives only the late backup and the courier deadline leaves the holder unanswered; credit recognizing that and asking who carried the card (EX-2). Expansive, informal context is style, not evasion.
dimension_notes.evidence_based_followup: Credit requesting rec-01 and rec-02 as soon as they open (exchange 5), then rec-03 and rec-04, and putting the holder entry and the person counts to the subject.
dimension_notes.testing_alternatives: Credit testing the second-holder account (a:01) against the single-person account (a:02) before closing, and checking a:03 against rec-06 and doc-02.
dimension_notes.supported_closure: Truthful closure cites rec-01 with rec-02, or rec-04 with rec-03, together with Strand's account that Grell carried and presented SP-3. Before exchange 5, 'insufficient evidence' naming rec-01 and rec-02 is expected (EX-3).

turn_label_guide.situation: Answers 'What was SP-3 released for?' by describing the late backup and Hester's call before saying the card was for Tobias.
turn_label_guide.label: responsive
turn_label_guide.rationale: Expansive, informal style puts context first; the purpose is free to disclose and he gives it in the same answer. An assistant should not flag the context as evasion.

turn_label_guide.situation: Says he and Tobias left the vault at about ten to ten, and that he did not see Tobias put SP-3 back.
turn_label_guide.label: genuine_uncertainty
turn_label_guide.rationale: Within uncertainty limits u:01 and u:02.

turn_label_guide.situation: Cannot say why Tobias's renewal had not been entered or what the overnight report shows.
turn_label_guide.label: genuine_uncertainty

turn_label_guide.situation: Gives a partial answer to a question that bundles the spare card, the reader and the courier.
turn_label_guide.label: poorly_framed_question
turn_label_guide.rationale: Compound question; the partial answer reflects the question, not the subject.

Each presents a different credential at the two-credential reader, and both stay until the work is finished and leave together. (b) No person may present more than one credential at the reader. (c) Spare cards are kept in the NOC key cabinet, which releases a card only against the PIN of a person whose badge opens TV-1. A certified operator may release a spare card for a certified colleague whose own badge will not open TV-1, and must write the holder's name, the time and the reason on the paper spare-card register. The holder keeps the card until it is returned to the cabinet.

evaluator_packet.synopsis: Grell's TV-1 access came off his badge at 18:00 in the quarterly review, an entry backlog on an approved renewal, and Grell went home at 20:32. The weekly backup finished at 20:41; at 20:45 Vane, off site, phoned and asked Strand to pull the 14 courier tapes before the 22:00 pickup, and Strand did not tell her Grell had gone. Wanting to avoid a second missed courier after a written reminder, Strand released spare card SP-3 under his own PIN, wrote nothing on the paper register and at 21:14 presented his own badge and SP-3 himself at the two-credential reader. He pulled the tapes alone, left at 21:51, the courier collected them at 21:58 and he returned the card at 22:05. Distractors shared with the truthful variant: Grell's lapsed access and the evening timing; here the reconciliation's attribution of both credentials to Strand is accurate.

decisive_support.description: The door camera counted one person in at 21:14 and one out at 21:51 while two credentials opened the door, and the paper register names no holder for SP-3; Strand gives no account of who presented the second credential when asked.
The badge events show Grell leaving through the lobby at 20:32, and Grell states he went home before the tape pull, was never in TV-1 that night and had no spare card.

dimension_notes.clarity_neutrality: Credit open, single questions about the spare card and the people at the reader. 'Why did you use two cards?' presumes that one person presented both credentials.
dimension_notes.response_relevance: An answer to 'What was SP-3 released for?' that gives only the late backup and the courier deadline leaves the holder unanswered; credit recognizing that and asking who carried the card (EX-2). Expansive, informal context is style, not evasion.
dimension_notes.evidence_based_followup: Credit requesting rec-01 and rec-02 as soon as they open (exchange 5), then rec-03 and rec-04, and putting the holder entry and the person counts to the subject.
dimension_notes.testing_alternatives: Credit testing the second-holder account (a:01) against the single-person account (a:02) before closing, and checking a:03 against rec-06 and doc-02.
dimension_notes.supported_closure: Deceptive closure cites rec-02 and rec-01 (one person in and out, no holder on the register) with Strand's non-answers on who presented SP-3, or rec-03 with rec-04. Calm, expansive answers are never grounds.
